Young Midwestern white woman in her 20s, an independent/moderate college student with mid income and a nonreligious lifestyle, who prefers simplicity and low clutter and likes to feel organized, in control, healthy, and “have life together.” Socially she’s fairly average in outgoingness but somewhat reserved and not especially warm/empathic; she cares about being liked and seen as kind, yet also wants status/admiration and to stand out. Male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, never married, lives alone, works full-time on a low income; atheist, politically independent but socially/liberally oriented. Strong preference for simplicity/minimalism and clear mental budgeting; financially cautious and risk-averse, not prone to impulsive spending, with average practical numeracy/financial knowledge.

Married, retired White woman in her 50s–60s living in the Northeast; conservative/Republican, culturally Protestant but not very observant, financially comfortable and highly financially literate. Decision-wise she’s practical and organized when she commits, but can be inconsistent with routine self-discipline; she’s relatively comfortable with ambiguity and doesn’t need quick closure, and she sometimes prefers standing out rather than blending in. She’s moderately pro-environment, not minimalist, and can be somewhat spendy/impulse-prone despite strong money knowledge.

White male (30–49) in the U.S. South, postgraduate-educated, single and living alone, employed full-time with mid income; politically moderate/independent and culturally Buddhist but non-practicing. Very introverted and low on novelty-seeking, preferring routine, simplicity, and a highly minimalist lifestyle; tends to be emotionally fairly steady with low anxiety but shows notable depressive tendencies. Young Hispanic man in the U.S. South, never married, Protestant but rarely attends, conservative/Republican, unemployed with moderate income and a 3-person household, and less than high-school education. Married, high-earning West Coast woman in her 20s with postgraduate education; very liberal Democrat, agnostic, and strongly environmentally minded. Young Southern U.S. woman (late teens–20s) with an associate’s degree, living with a partner in a small household, working full-time on a low income; politically moderate/independent and lightly religious. Married Black Catholic woman in the Midwest (30–49), high-school educated, working full-time on a low income in a 3-person household; politically independent but conservative and highly involved in church. Divorced white woman in her 50s–60s in the US West with an associate’s degree, unemployed, moderate income, atheist, and very liberal/Democrat. Financially and numerically average, somewhat impatient about delayed rewards, not minimalist (comfortable with more possessions/variety), moderately eco-leaning, and empathetic with a strong desire to leave things better than she found them.

Widowed Hispanic man in his 30s–40s living in the US South; self-employed, high-income, high-school educated, weekly religious attendee, and politically conservative/Republican. Midwestern white male (30–49), divorced, agnostic, politically moderate/independent, highly educated and high-earning, working full-time in a household of four. Married Black man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western US, highly educated and high-income, working full-time and supporting a large household; Protestant who attends church occasionally and frames identity around being a faithful, loving, and financially responsible family leader. Socially confident, outgoing, cooperative, and highly disciplined/organized, with very low anxiety/depressive tendency and a clear, stable sense of self. Practical and tradition-leaning rather than novelty-seeking, prefers simplicity/minimalism, and likes clear answers and closure; adapts his presentation to context and is attentive to social norms (may answer in a socially desirable way). Moderately pro-environment and politically moderate Democrat. Married Southern white woman (30–49), high-income and postgraduate educated, working full-time as a driven, detail-oriented CRNA; very conservative Republican and deeply involved in Protestant church life. Numerically strong and practical, but less inclined toward abstract deliberation and can be overconfident in her judgments; money behavior skews tight/reluctant to spend despite comfort with strategic generosity and trust when reciprocity is expected. Environmentally minded and community-oriented, balancing ambition with duty, faith-based values, and a desire to make a meaningful positive impact.

Unemployed Hispanic woman in her 30s–40s in the Northeast, low income, high‑school educated, very liberal Democrat and nonreligious, living in a two‑person household. Married Hispanic man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western U.S., high‑school educated, part‑time employed with a solid middle income; culturally Catholic but rarely attends, and strongly liberal/Democrat. Midwest-based woman in her 50s–early 60s, college educated, Protestant and weekly churchgoer, politically independent but conservative, living in a two-person household with low income and currently unemployed. Young Hispanic Catholic woman in the U.S. South (18–29), moderate Democrat, part-time worker with an associate’s degree, living in a 4-person household and is a mother; values family/community and shows strong empathy, fairness, and generosity, tending to share evenly and to trust others while also being somewhat cautious about being treated unfairly. Spending is slightly tightwad-leaning and uses mental “budgets” to organize gains/losses; aspires to be more confident, well-spoken, successful, and—given parenting responsibilities—more patient, responsible, and selfless.

Married Hispanic Catholic woman (30–49) in the Western US with postgraduate education, a homemaker in a four-person household and moderate/independent politics. Male in his 50s–60s, Asian, West US, self-employed with low income, never married, agnostic/nonreligious, very conservative Republican. Self-employed, high-income Asian American man in his 50s–60s living in the US South; postgraduate educated, divorced, nonreligious, politically moderate/independent, in a two-person household. Young Asian American woman in the Western US (late teens/20s), college-educated, liberal/Democrat, atheist, currently unemployed and living in a large household. Young Asian American man in the Southern US, part-time employed with some college, moderate Democrat, loosely practicing Buddhist, living alone. Midwestern married white man (30–49) with an associate’s degree, high income, Protestant (attends monthly), politically independent but conservative. Black male in his 50s living in the US South, self-employed with some college, moderate income, never married, liberal/Democrat and nonreligious. Young Black woman in the South, high-income household, student, moderate Democrat with low religious identification but weekly attendance; socially outgoing in comfortable settings yet shy about public speaking and wants to become more outspoken, optimistic, and high-achieving (straight-A, big-organization career, eventual business).
